content: The Water and Sanitation for Health Facility Improvement Tool (WASH FIT), developed by WHO and UNICEF, is a risk-based framework designed to enhance and sustain water, sanitation, hygiene, and healthcare waste management services in healthcare facilities. It provides a structured, continuous process for assessing and prioritizing risks, implementing improvements, and monitoring progress. The tool focuses on four key areas: water, sanitation (including healthcare waste), hygiene (such as hand hygiene and environmental cleaning), and general management. WASH FIT integrates improvement activities into existing infection prevention and control (IPC) and quality improvement efforts within healthcare facilities. It is adapted from the Water Safety Plan (WSP) and Sanitation Safety Planning (SSP) approaches recommended in WHO guidelines for drinking water quality and sanitation and health. The WASH FIT guide is available in multiple languages, including Arabic, English, French, Russian, and Spanish. Since its introduction in 2015, WASH FIT has been implemented in over 20 countries, including pilot projects in Tajikistan, Mali, and Liberia. While primarily used in non-emergency settings, it has also been applied in emergency contexts, such as in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, where it was used to assess and improve over 200 healthcare facilities. Additionally, it has been utilized in peacekeeping and military settings, such as in South Sudan, to improve water, wastewater, and waste management systems, benefiting over 20,000 individuals. The implementation of WASH FIT involves three main stages: preparation, implementation and action, and follow-up and evaluation. During the preparation phase, a situational analysis is conducted to understand the broader context and resource requirements. Improvements in WASH infrastructure and services are budgeted and aligned with national policies and standards to ensure sustainability. The implementation phase follows a five-step process: forming a team, conducting an assessment, prioritizing risks and developing an improvement plan, making incremental improvements, and monitoring and revising the plan. Follow-up often requires technical support from external sources, and regular visits by government or supporting partners are essential for data collection and evaluation. WASH FIT training modules are available online in English, French, and Russian. These modules are adaptable to local contexts and include materials for conducting training sessions, such as sample agendas, evaluation sheets, and preand post-training quizzes. The tool also facilitates real-time tracking of progress and enables facility teams to share solutions to challenges or engage in friendly competitions. In addition to WASH FIT, other tools such as the WASH Bottleneck Analysis Tool (WASH BAT), the Clean Clinic Approach (CCA), and the WASH & CLEAN Toolkit are available to support WASH improvements in healthcare facilities. These tools provide frameworks for baseline assessments, monitoring, evaluation, and advocacy, and they emphasize the integration of WASH activities into broader quality of care initiatives.
